visual_action: A rapid montage of several different viral video clips of people looking extremely distressed. The first clip shows a young person screaming while holding their head. The second shows a close-up of a Black man crying. The third shows a Black woman screaming in a bathroom. The final clips show a bald white man with a cigarette looking dejected, with a brief cross-fade of a woman with glasses looking stressed.

spoken_summary: The audio consists of lyrics from the Kelly Clarkson song "Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You)", including the lines "What doesn't kill you makes you stronger, stand a little taller."
audio_music: The video is set to the upbeat, anthemic pop song "Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You)" by Kelly Clarkson. The triumphant and empowering tone of the music is used ironically, juxtaposed with visuals of people in extreme distress.
editing_pacing: The video uses fast cuts, presenting a rapid montage of different short clips in a slideshow or meme compilation style.
cultural_references: The song "Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You)" by Kelly Clarkson.
The format uses a series of viral internet videos and reaction clips, including the well-known 'crying man' meme, to represent an emotional breakdown.
The premise of the meme refers to leaked audio from 2018 in which Melania Trump expressed frustration with her First Lady duties, specifically decorating for Christmas.
central_claim: Melania Trump dreads her responsibility of decorating for Christmas, viewing it as a torturous obligation.
intended_effect: To mock Melania Trump and amuse the viewer by referencing her past controversial comments about Christmas decorations.
